words.sense: An exemplary or original model of a person or thing that others seem to copy.
misconceptions: A typical example need not be a sweeping belief.

words.sense: A rigid, oversimplified belief imposed on a group.
misconceptions: A claim about everyone is not an exemplary individual.

semantic_axes.description: Exemplary individual or original pattern versus oversimplified group-level belief.

edges.boundary_rule: An archetype is an exemplary instance or model, whereas a stereotype is a rigid generalization about members of a group.
clues_a: an individual embodying a familiar pattern
a design that becomes the template
clues_b: one trait attributed to all members
irrelevant_clues: how many people saw the message

misconceptions.M1: Mistakes an exemplary person or original pattern for a claim about a whole group.
misconceptions.M2: Treats a blanket generalization as if it were a representative individual.
misconceptions.M3: Assumes a flattering group generalization cannot be fixed or misleading.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Amina’s portrayal of the club mentor?

beats.text: Amina shows one mentor welcoming newcomers, sharing credit, and guiding others; new volunteers copy the character’s habits.
beats.decisive_clue: one exemplary mentor serves as a model
beats.reason: The first detail establishes one exemplary mentor serves as a model; that is the meaningful distinction.

beats.text: The same character appears on every training poster as the example future mentors should follow.
beats.decisive_clue: the single mentor is the pattern others copy
beats.reason: The new detail confirms the single mentor is the pattern others copy and rules out the competing sense.

chains.feedback_short: The character is a model others follow, not a blanket claim about mentors.
chains.feedback_deep: Archetype means an exemplary model or typical original. Stereotype means a fixed oversimplification about a group. Here, the portrayed mentor provides a concrete ideal, not a claim that all mentors behave identically.
chains.contrast_rule: A model represents a kind; a stereotype makes a rigid claim about a group.

hints.attention: Notice whether this is one model or a claim about everyone.
hints.axis: Exemplary individual or original pattern versus oversimplified group-level belief.
hints.contrast: A model represents a kind; a stereotype makes a rigid claim about a group.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Felix’s comment about bargain hunters?

beats.text: Felix writes, “Every discount shopper buys things they never need,” without asking anyone about their purchases.
beats.decisive_clue: a blanket claim about all discount shoppers
beats.reason: The first detail establishes a blanket claim about all discount shoppers; that is the meaningful distinction.

beats.text: His comment spreads through several shopping chats, but its claim still covers every bargain hunter.
beats.decisive_clue: the original blanket claim persists despite wider circulation
beats.reason: The deciding fact remains a blanket claim about all discount shoppers; the added detail does not change that.

chains.feedback_short: Circulation changes nothing: the comment still assigns one habit to a whole group.
chains.feedback_deep: Archetype means an exemplary model or typical original. Stereotype means a fixed oversimplification about a group. Here, popularity does not make a fixed judgment about an entire group into an exemplary instance.
chains.contrast_rule: A model represents a kind; a stereotype makes a rigid claim about a group.

hints.attention: Look at the scope of the claim, not its audience.
hints.axis: Exemplary individual or original pattern versus oversimplified group-level belief.
hints.contrast: A model represents a kind; a stereotype makes a rigid claim about a group.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Kavi’s assumption about reserve players?

beats.text: After one substitute misses a shot, Kavi says everyone on the bench lacks courage.
beats.decisive_clue: one incident became a judgment about an entire group
beats.reason: The first detail establishes one incident became a judgment about an entire group; that is the meaningful distinction.

beats.text: He keeps the same view even after watching a substitute take the deciding penalty.
beats.decisive_clue: evidence against the broad judgment did not alter it
beats.reason: The new detail confirms evidence against the broad judgment did not alter it and rules out the competing sense.

chains.feedback_short: One missed shot becomes a rule for everyone, even after contrary evidence.
chains.feedback_deep: Archetype means an exemplary model or typical original. Stereotype means a fixed oversimplification about a group. Here, a single missed shot is being used to label all reserves, and a contrary example fails to loosen that belief.
chains.contrast_rule: A model represents a kind; a stereotype makes a rigid claim about a group.

hints.attention: Ask whether the claim describes one player or all reserves.
hints.axis: Exemplary individual or original pattern versus oversimplified group-level belief.
hints.contrast: A model represents a kind; a stereotype makes a rigid claim about a group.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Ines’s character in her family story?

beats.text: Ines creates a wise aunt whose advice and patience make her the example that younger characters try to match.
beats.decisive_clue: the aunt is a single exemplary character
beats.reason: The first detail establishes the aunt is a single exemplary character; that is the meaningful distinction.

beats.text: The aunt wears a bright yellow coat in every chapter.
beats.decisive_clue: the same exemplary character remains despite a distinctive coat
beats.reason: The deciding fact remains the aunt is a single exemplary character; the added detail does not change that.

chains.feedback_short: Her role as an example matters; the coat does not change that role.
chains.feedback_deep: Archetype means an exemplary model or typical original. Stereotype means a fixed oversimplification about a group. Here, the coat is memorable, but it says nothing about assigning traits to everyone in a group.
chains.contrast_rule: A model represents a kind; a stereotype makes a rigid claim about a group.

hints.attention: Focus on what the other characters do because of her.
hints.axis: Exemplary individual or original pattern versus oversimplified group-level belief.
hints.contrast: A model represents a kind; a stereotype makes a rigid claim about a group.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Ravi’s picture of the ideal explorer?

beats.text: Ravi draws one traveler who prepares carefully, helps companions, and stays calm when plans change.
beats.decisive_clue: a single idealized traveler embodies a type
beats.reason: The first detail establishes a single idealized traveler embodies a type; that is the meaningful distinction.

beats.text: For the book’s later chapters, every new explorer is designed by adapting Ravi’s original figure.
beats.decisive_clue: the same drawing also becomes the template for later travelers
beats.reason: Viewed in its fuller context, the same drawing also becomes the template for later travelers; the original distinction still decides it.

chains.feedback_short: Later characters are built from this one model, rather than judged as a group.
chains.feedback_deep: Archetype means an exemplary model or typical original. Stereotype means a fixed oversimplification about a group. Here, the drawing is not about attributing one presumed trait to all real travelers; it offers a pattern for characters.
chains.contrast_rule: A model represents a kind; a stereotype makes a rigid claim about a group.

hints.attention: Consider how the picture is used later.
hints.axis: Exemplary individual or original pattern versus oversimplified group-level belief.
hints.contrast: A model represents a kind; a stereotype makes a rigid claim about a group.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Zoe’s claim about members of the garden club?

beats.text: Zoe says everyone in the garden club cares more about awards than plants, though she has met only two members.
beats.decisive_clue: limited encounters support a sweeping group belief
beats.reason: The first detail establishes limited encounters support a sweeping group belief; that is the meaningful distinction.

beats.text: She phrases the claim as a compliment about ambition, but still assigns the same motive to every member.
beats.decisive_clue: the claim still assigns the same motive to every member
beats.reason: The deciding fact remains limited encounters support a sweeping group belief; the added detail does not change that.

chains.feedback_short: A compliment can still impose one untested motive on an entire group.
chains.feedback_deep: Archetype means an exemplary model or typical original. Stereotype means a fixed oversimplification about a group. Here, a flattering tone can still conceal an oversimplified assumption about a group.
chains.contrast_rule: A model represents a kind; a stereotype makes a rigid claim about a group.
